product.name: COMPACT BOXY FIT HOODIE
product.pageTitle: COMPACT BOXY FIT HOODIE - Eggplant | ZARA United States

fit.brandWords: Boxy fit hoodie in compact, double-knit cotton.

material.composition: Outer shell: 100% cotton / Lining (main fabric): 100% polyester / Hood: 100% cotton
material.source: product page, Composition & care. Zara does not say how much the fabric stretches.

garment.label: Product Measurements, Product dimensions (CM): "The garment is measured flat"

methodSource.says: How a garment is measured: "CHEST — Measure from side to side at armhole height." Product dimensions: "The garment is measured flat".

derivedCircumference.derivation: Zara measures the garment flat, side to side at armhole height: a width, not a circumference. Where Fynd needs the chest around, it takes 2 × the published flat width and labels it estimated; the derived value is never stored here.

methodSource.says: How a garment is measured: "FRONT LENGTH — Measure from the shoulder seam to the bottom hem of the garment." Recorded as from the high point of the shoulder, where the shoulder seam meets the collar; Zara does not say which point of the seam.
How a garment is measured: "SLEEVE LENGTH — Measure from the shoulder/sleeve seam to the hem of the sleeve."
How a garment is measured: "BACK WIDTH — Measure from the shoulder/sleeve seam to the other shoulder/sleeve seam."

sources.what: product page (reference 8054/370): Description, Composition & care, Product Measurements (cm and in) and How a garment is measured

notes: Sold under MAN; the product's offers list S, M, L, XL.
Recorded in centimetres, Zara's own values; its inch table is the same numbers converted to one decimal.
Zara publishes the finished garment only, no body chart. "Arm circumference" is published but not recorded (no such dimension in the schema).
Construction: Zara does not say whether the sleeves are set-in, raglan or dropped, so construction.sleeve is unknown.

NEEDS APPROVAL: back width (68.5-71.5 cm) is wider than the chest (63-69 cm), which points to dropped shoulders; Zara does not say so. With the shoulder seam on the upper arm, its back width and sleeve are not comparable with a set-in garment's, even though both are measured "seam to seam" and "from the seam".
"Boxy fit" is mapped to the oversized fit class.
